cases.title: Van Dusen v. Barrack
cases.holding: A defendant's § 1404(a) convenience transfer of a properly brought diversity action preserves the transferor forum's governing state law, including its choice-of-law rules.
cases.applicationLimits: Proper initial venue and jurisdiction matter. The decision concerns § 1404(a), not every MDL direct-filing scenario.

cases.title: Ferens v. John Deere Co.
cases.holding: The transferor-law rule for § 1404(a) convenience transfers also applies when the plaintiff requests the transfer.
cases.applicationLimits: Does not supply a state's accrual or tolling law or a nationwide direct-filing rule.

cases.title: Lexecon Inc. v. Milberg Weiss Bershad Hynes & Lerach
cases.holding: A court handling § 1407 pretrial proceedings could not use § 1404(a) to assign the transferred case to itself for trial instead of the statutory remand.
cases.applicationLimits: Concerns transferred cases and trial assignment. It does not create a limitations period or establish registry tolling.

cases.title: Menowitz v. Brown
cases.court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit
cases.holding: The court distinguished preservation of state substantive law and choice-of-law rules in transferred litigation from the transferee court's interpretation of federal law.
cases.applicationLimits: The underlying claims were federal securities claims. A borrowed state period for a federal cause of action can become a federal-law question.

cases.title: Atlantic Marine Construction Co. v. U.S. District Court
cases.holding: The usual § 1404(a) transferor choice-of-law retention does not apply to a transfer enforcing a valid forum-selection clause against a party that filed elsewhere.
cases.applicationLimits: Review the clause, validity, transfer basis and covered claims. This exception does not substitute the MDL state's law in every transferred claim.

cases.title: Dobbs v. DePuy Orthopedics, Inc.
cases.court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit
cases.holding: For the foreign direct-filed MDL action before it, the court treated the identified originating forum as relevant to choice of law rather than automatically using the MDL forum's law.
cases.applicationLimits: The immediate dispute involved attorney compensation. The Seventh Circuit reasoning requires the particular filing facts and is not a universal direct-filing order.

cases.title: Looper / Lambert v. Cook Incorporated
cases.court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit
cases.holding: In the Cook IVC-filter MDL, the court relied on the defendant's case-specific consent and prior positions to use originating jurisdictions' choice-of-law rules for direct-filed cases.
cases.applicationLimits: The court expressly limits the result to the unusual facts. Direct-filing orders, originating venue, consent and changes of position must be reviewed.

cases.title: Hazine v. Montgomery Elevator Co.
cases.holding: The court held that § 12-551 could not constitutionally extinguish the strict product-liability claim before the injury, overruling Bryant's contrary result.
cases.applicationLimits: Do not convert the still-published twelve-year language into an operative automatic repose cutoff. Later law and the precise claim require review.

cases.title: Commonwealth v. Neiman
cases.holding: The court struck Act 152 of 2004 in its entirety for violating the state constitution's single-subject rule and stayed the result for ninety days.
cases.applicationLimits: The official Chapter 55 publisher flags the resulting invalidity of asbestos amendments. Published § 5524.1 or added § 5524(8) text alone cannot authorize an automatic asbestos trigger.

cases.title: Myers v. Crouse-Hinds Division of Cooper Industries, Inc.
cases.holding: The court found § 34-20-3-2's disparate treatment of asbestos plaintiffs unconstitutional and concluded the product repose statute did not bar the plaintiffs' protracted-exposure claims.
cases.applicationLimits: This does not erase ordinary Indiana product repose for every product. Subsequent treatment and the particular exposure theory require review.

cases.title: Fox v. Ethicon Endo-Surgery, Inc.
cases.copyPublisher: Justia reproduction of primary court opinion
cases.holding: Product claims under negligence or strict liability may have delayed accrual. Suspicion of a factual basis and a reasonable investigation matter; knowledge of medical negligence does not automatically establish discovery of a different product wrongdoing. Footnote 3 identifies the then-current two-year injury statute, CCP § 335.1.
cases.applicationLimits: The claim arose under the former one-year statute. This reference supports the discovery analysis and distinction of claims, not automatic use of diagnosis, device removal or defendant identification as the trigger. Later treatment and special exposure statutes require separate review.

cases.title: Best v. Taylor Machine Works, Inc.
cases.copyPublisher: Justia reproduction of primary court opinion
cases.holding: The court held Public Act 89-7 void in its entirety because the invalid core provisions could not be severed. The Illinois publisher therefore distinguishes the product statute with those changes from the version without them.
cases.applicationLimits: The invalid expanded version of § 13-213 must not supply an all-theories repose rule. Apply claim classification and the unaffected statutory text after current-law and subsequent-treatment review.

cases.title: Dickie v. Farmers Union Oil Co. of LaMoure
cases.copyPublisher: Justia public HTML copy of the North Dakota Supreme Court opinion
cases.holding: The 1995 product-repose classification in N.D.C.C. §28-01.3-08 violated N.D. Const. art. I, §21. The court reaffirmed Hanson and rejected the 10-year purchase / 11-year manufacture bar.
cases.applicationLimits: The certified question addressed the product-repose classification, not a comprehensive adjudication of each asbestos exception or every present-day claim. Published §28-01.3-08 text is preserved as evidence, not promoted to an operative calculator rule.
cases.subsequentTreatment: No comprehensive current subsequent-treatment or severability review completed; no automatic product-repose or asbestos period emitted.
